No system action is needed for this capability.
Open the accessibility list, find Phone assistant, and turn the service on. Reading the screen and performing gestures both require it.
Gestures only reach the default display, and screenshot without a system prompt requires Android 11 or later.
Install Shizuku, start it by wireless debugging or through a computer, then return here and grant this app access. Privileged operations run as the shell identity and require it.
Shizuku is not running. Privileged capabilities stay blocked until its service is detected.

Notification access has its own system page. Screen capture depends on the path: in the foreground the system confirms every time, in the background this app takes the frames itself with no system dialog. Media access is requested on this page.
Adds an argument digest to each entry. Keep it off unless a fault is being reproduced.
Written to the Phone assistant run log; rotates once it passes 2 MB
One line per call: capability, both gates, decision, target and duration. Argument values are stored only as a salted digest.
Kept for 30 days; expired files are removed automatically
A call is in flight. Try again after it finishes.

Artifacts delivered to DSH land in /opt/pilot/out (shots, recordings, audio, other files). The output directory keeps the latest 20 per kind, up to 256 MB and 7 days; anything modified in the last 10 minutes is never collected. The 24-hour rule and the artifact quota apply to the host-side delivery copies.
The guide has not been generated yet. Start the sandbox first.

Open the Cordis panel and turn on the "DSH Phone Link" switch to install the phone-control plugin.
Send this line to DSH in the sandbox and it will start using the tools:
Read /opt/pilot/USAGE.md, then call /opt/pilot/bin/pilot as it says.

The prompt has three possible homes, in this order: inside the Phone assistant screen whenever that screen is in front; above everything else when it is not and this grant is given; and the notification shade - pull it down and tap Allow - when it is not. With notifications blocked as well there is nothing left to tap.
Assistant artifacts (each auto-collected on its own schedule)
%1$s needs the accessibility service, and the system no longer lists this app among the enabled services: the permission was switched off. Switch it back on.

%1$s needs the accessibility service. The system still lists this app, so the permission was not revoked: the app was closed in the background. Reopening this app is enough, no setting has to be changed.
The system still lists this app, but the service is not bound right now: the app was closed in the background. Reopen this app to bring the screen capabilities back.
The system can close this app at any moment; when it does, the accessibility service is unbound and every screen capability stops at once. These are the switches a normal app can reach.
This device offers no entry to that page from here. Find it in the system settings by hand.

The auto-start and background-run page is written by the device maker and has no public entry point. This app tries the component names known for your brand in order and opens the first one that actually starts; when none does, it falls back to manual steps. Switch names and nesting change between ROM versions, and on devices that have not been verified against real hardware the page may sit elsewhere.

Lets the assistant read the current screen and perform gestures and text entry on your behalf (taps, long presses, swipes, scrolling, setting control values and keys). The system grants this service once; the assistant itself still asks for each capability one by one, and it never controls this app.
Installs through Shizuku, which may still need the user to confirm. Always asks.

Records the screen. Recording the screen in front of the user needs system consent each time; the background screen is captured frame by frame by the assistant and needs none.
Needs Shizuku and Android 13 or later.

"Sends a fixed system shortcut: set an alarm or timer, open the alarm or timer screen, a system settings page, an app's details page, the dial pad (it never dials) or a browser page. Needs neither accessibility nor Shizuku. Only the templates in the table are accepted, out-of-range arguments are refused, there is no entry that deletes or cancels an alarm, and nothing is sent while this app is in the background without the overlay permission."
Writes protected settings through Shizuku. Always asks.
"Controls the phone with system-level permissions. Includes read-only verbs and some basic ones by default."
